- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast peak at +5% above spike or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in recognizing momentum; add 1–2% upward bias in 3rd–5th day of forecast window.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often underestimates reversal; add 1–2% upward bias in 6th–8th day.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overestimate volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% in mid-horizon (days 10–15).
- If official event (e.g., policy change, auction) occurs within 3 days, model often misses timing; adjust forecast to align with event date +1–2 days, then apply sentiment-weighted correction.
